note: Researched recommendations, written in the site's voice but by somebody who has not been. Opinionated on purpose — a list of facts is not a guide — but every card says plainly that it was researched rather than visited, and a handwritten note in notes.json overrules any of it. This file exists because nothing else can fill it: Wikidata holds three cafes in the whole of Bengaluru and no open dataset in India describes everyday food. See SOURCES.md.
rules: Every record needs a source and a lastVerified date. If it cannot be checked, it does not go in.
Say what to order and when to go. 'Lovely atmosphere' helps nobody.
No opening hours in prose. OpenStreetMap carries them, js/hours.js reads them, and a time written here is a time that rots.
quality and uniqueness cap at 4 here. 5 is reserved for somewhere one of you actually loved.
Always pin `match` with a zone. A chain with fourteen branches will otherwise resolve to whichever one the index happened to list first.

items.title: Vidyarthi Bhavan
items.why: Gandhi Bazaar since 1943, opened to feed students at the National College up the road — Vidyarthi Bhavan means student house. The benne masala dosa is the order and it is fried in enough butter to be a decision. Expect to give your name, wait on the pavement and share a table. Go on a weekday morning; weekends are a different and worse experience.
items.source: Wikipedia; Karnataka Tourism; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Mavalli Tiffin Rooms
items.why: Founded in 1924 by two brothers from Udupi as the Brahmins' Coffee Club on Lalbagh Fort Road, MTR is known for popularising the rava idli. Order that, and the filter coffee.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Koshy's
items.why: A family-run café where Nehru, Queen Elizabeth II and Khrushchev have eaten, and where journalists and writers still gather. Order tea and something off the old menu.

items.title: Shree Sagar CTR
items.why: Central Tiffin Room, or Sri Sagar, a Malleswaram restaurant from the 1920s famous for its masala dosa, with or without butter. Get the butter one.

items.title: Lalbagh Botanical Gardens
items.why: Hyder Ali's garden from 1760, later run by British superintendents, with a glass house from 1890 that still holds the flower shows around Republic and Independence Days.

items.title: Cubbon Park
items.why: The city's central park, officially Sri Chamarajendra Park, named after commissioner Sir Mark Cubbon. Walk it in the morning.

items.title: Champaca Bookstore, Library & Cafe
items.why: A bookshop run by booksellers who post their own recommendations, with a children's library and a café. Browse, then sit with a coffee.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Blossom Book House
items.why: A bookshop with shelves across almost every subject, from fiction and history to Kannada novels and author-signed copies. Give yourself an hour.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Toit
items.why: The Indiranagar brewpub that brews its own range, from Tint-in-Wit to Basmati Blonde and a nitro stout. Order a taster of the house beers.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Ulsoor Lake Park
items.why: Ulsoor Lake, one of the city's biggest lakes, near MG Road, spread over fifty hectares with several islands. Walk the edge at sunset.
items.imageCredit: Ramesh NG from Bangalore, INDIA · CC BY-SA 2.0

items.title: City Market
items.why: K R Market, the city's largest wholesale market and one of Asia's biggest flower markets, beside Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace. Go early for the flowers.

items.title: Albert Bakery
items.why: A Fraser Town bakery on Mosque Road, founded in 1902 and named after Prince Albert, known for savoury snacks and, during Ramzan, its brain puffs.

items.title: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters
items.why: A café of the Indian roaster that buys from more than eighty coffee estates and smallholders. Ask what single estate is on the bar.

items.title: Brahmin's Coffee Bar
items.why: A Basavanagudi tiffin bar from 1965, one of the old vegetarian eating houses that came before the city's darshinis. Stand at the counter for idli, vada and coffee.

items.title: Lavonne Café
items.why: The café of Lavonne, a baking and pastry academy teaching since 2012, so the pastries are the point. Come for breakfast.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Kopitiam Lah
items.why: India's first kopitiam, a Malaysian coffee shop and eatery in the tradition of Malaysia's old coffee houses. Order a kopi.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Yauatcha
items.why: The Bengaluru branch of the Soho dim sum teahouse, in MG Road Mall, open all day. Order dim sum and something from the patisserie.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Malgudi Mylari Mane
items.why: A Karnataka restaurant serving traditional vegetarian and non-vegetarian food, with branches in Koramangala and on the Mangalore highway.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Bier Library
items.why: A Koramangala brewpub built around its own craft beer and a comfortable room. Order a flight.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Pizza 4P's
items.why: The Indian branch of Pizza 4P's, the pizza restaurant that began in Vietnam. Order a pizza to share.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: KOKO
items.why: An Asian gastropub with branches in Mumbai and Hyderabad, and a bar in its Bengaluru room. Book for dinner and cocktails.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Arbor Brewing Company
items.why: India's first American craft brewery, opened in 2012 and one of the breweries the city's beer scene is known for. Ask what is new on tap.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: 6oz Coffee and Roasters
items.why: A neighbourhood specialty coffee shop on Tank Road, Ulsoor, pouring espresso drinks, pour-overs and cold brew made with Indian beans.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Krumb Kraft
items.why: A sourdough bakehouse making breads, crackers, cakes and preserves without additives. Buy a loaf.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Amintiri
items.why: A bakery for celebration cakes, loaf cakes and French-style viennoiserie, with a café in HSR Layout. Order a pastry.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Nasi and Mee
items.why: A Southeast Asian restaurant for nasi, ramen, sushi and dim sum. Order a nasi goreng.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Reservoire
items.why: A big Koramangala cocktail bar, opened in 2017 to bring a Manhattan-style cocktail culture to the city. Sit at the bar.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Oota Bangalore
items.why: A restaurant built on hyper-local Karnataka cooking, named after the Kannada greeting 'Oota aita?' — have you eaten? Order across the regions of the state.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lavonne
items.why: The Whitefield café of Lavonne, a baking and pastry academy teaching since 2012. Come in the morning for pastries and bread.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lakeview Milk Bar
items.why: An ice-cream parlour that has been part of the city since before Independence. Order a sundae.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters
items.why: A café of the Indian roaster that buys from more than eighty coffee estates and smallholders. Ask what single estate is on the bar.

items.title: The Rameshwaram Cafe
items.why: A large-format darshini with ordering kiosks, one of the newcomers reshaping the city's standing-room South Indian eateries. Order at the kiosk and eat standing.

items.title: Bengaluru Cafe
items.why: A newer darshini with rustic interiors and a more modern look than the old eating houses. Order a dosa at the counter.

items.title: Taaza Thindi
items.why: A Jayanagar darshini, one of the newer, rustic-looking standing-room eateries. Order idli, vada and coffee at the counter.

items.title: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters
items.why: A café of the Indian roaster that buys from more than eighty coffee estates and smallholders. Ask what single estate is on the bar.

items.title: The Biere Club
items.why: A brewpub just off UB City inspired by a roomy British pub, with its own beers and food. Order a taster of the house brews.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Russel Market
items.why: The Cantonment's covered market, built by the British in 1927 and named for municipal commissioner T. B. Russell. Walk the produce and meat halls under the old roof, then out into Shivajinagar's streets.

items.title: Yeshwanthpur APMC Market
items.why: The city's biggest wholesale yard for farm produce. This is where Bengaluru's vegetables arrive, so go early, while the trading is on.

items.title: Murphy Town Market
items.why: Hoysala Nagara's neighbourhood market, known for its butchers and fishmongers, with one provisions shop, VM Stores, about a century old. One of the old Cantonment markets campaigners fought to save from demolition.

items.title: The Rameshwaram Cafe
items.source: therameshwaramcafe.org; address and hours from OpenStreetMap
items.why: A standing-room South Indian counter that started as street food in 2012 and became one of the city's busiest breakfasts. The order is ghee podi idli and a ghee masala dosa, then filter coffee. You pay at the till, collect at the counter and eat standing. Go early on a weekday, before the queue reaches the pavement.

items.title: Navathanyam
items.source: navathanyam.com; address and hours from OpenStreetMap
items.why: A South Indian kitchen built around the nine traditional grains, which makes it the place in Indiranagar to try millet in a full meal rather than as health food. Order the grain dishes you would not cook at home, and come at lunch, when the room is calmer.

items.title: Chinita
items.area: 218 Double Road, near the BDA Complex
items.why: Mexican food cooked from scratch since 2012, by a chef who learned it in New York and then in Mexico itself. It is the Mexican kitchen other Bengaluru restaurants are measured against. Order tacos and share plates, and book for a weekend dinner.

items.title: German BrezelHaus
items.why: A German craft bakery where every pretzel is shaped by hand, using some ingredients brought from Europe. Buy a pretzel and a sugar-dusted Berliner, or stay for a deli sandwich. It opens early enough on weekends to serve as the first stop on a Saturday morning.

items.title: Sharon Tea Stall
items.why: A local tea counter that now has twenty-five branches and claims a hundred kinds of tea. Skip the novelties and order a ginger-cardamom tea. Have it standing on the pavement, as the neighbourhood does, before the morning traffic starts.

items.title: Something's Brewing
items.why: Half café, half coffee shop for home brewers. It sells beans from several Indian roasters — Broot, Maverick & Farmer, Siolim — and the equipment to brew them. Have one cup, then take home whichever bag you liked.

items.title: The Kind
items.why: A vegetarian roastery with a brew room on 12th Main, so the coffee is roasted on the premises. Ask what is fresh off the roaster and have it as a pour-over.

items.title: Copper + Cloves
items.why: A plant-based kitchen that cooks seasonal produce from scratch. Healthy food usually tastes like a compromise; this tastes like lunch. Go for a weekday lunch and order a bowl.

items.title: Champaca
items.why: An independent bookshop, library and café chosen with a sharp eye for Indian writing and small presses. There are author readings and children's read-alouds, and weekends are laptop-free, which makes it a good place to read for an hour. Come for the Indian non-fiction shelf and ask the staff what to read next.

items.title: Atta Galatta
items.hoursNote: Events most weeks; the calendar is the timetable
items.why: A bookshop for Indian-language books with an events space attached. Atta Galatta runs the Bengaluru Poetry Festival and keeps a calendar of readings, film clubs and neighbourhood walks. Look at the calendar first and come for an event, then browse the Kannada shelves.

items.title: Manora
items.hoursNote: Hours not published — call before going
items.why: A commercial gallery on 100 Feet Road that runs changing exhibitions and keeps a stockroom of work for sale. It is a free half hour of contemporary art between meals. Check what is on before you go.

items.title: Goethe-Institut Max Müller Bhavan
items.why: The German cultural institute, in Bengaluru since 1961. It screens films and hosts concerts, exhibitions and talks, many of them free. The public library lends films, music and games as well as books. Check the events page for a screening, or spend a weekday afternoon in the library.

items.title: Indiranagar Sangeetha Sabha
items.area: Purandara Bhavana, 8th Main, 8th Cross, HAL 2nd Stage
items.hoursNote: Concerts by programme — the calendar is the timetable
items.why: A music and dance school founded in 1986, whose hall, Purandara Bhavana, was opened by A. P. J. Abdul Kalam in 2004. It is the neighbourhood's place for a Carnatic recital or a dance programme, and tickets are often cheap or free. Watch for the annual six-day music and dance festival.

items.title: Kaayal
items.area: 1647/1, 2nd floor, Jeevan Bhima Nagar Main Road, opposite Miranda School
items.why: A Kerala restaurant that has been a reliable choice on the Jeevan Bhima Nagar side of Old Airport Road for years. Order appam with stew, or a fish curry with rice, and come at lunch when the meals are on.

items.title: Jamavar
items.area: Lobby level, The Leela Palace, Old Airport Road
items.why: The Leela Palace's Indian dining room is decorated with gold-leaf paintings and silver place settings. The menu covers royal Indian cooking from across the country. Order the raan and the house dal, and book ahead for a special dinner.

items.title: The Registry of Sarees
items.why: A research centre for handspun and handwoven textiles with two collections, one of them a large study of khadi, and a reference library. It is open to the public by appointment only. Write ahead and say what you want to see, and you will get a quiet hour with the textiles themselves.

items.title: The Hole In The Wall Cafe

match.name: The Hole In The Wall Cafe

items.why: A Koramangala breakfast institution that began in 2009 as a no-frills garage. Order a full English breakfast or the pancakes, and get there before the weekend queue forms. It is closed on Mondays.

items.title: Kappa Chakka Kandhari
items.why: Kerala home and toddy-shop cooking, built from three years of research in 265 homes and 70 toddy shops, with Chef Regi Mathew in charge of the kitchen. Order kappa with the kodampuli fish curry and finish with the cloud pudding. Book for dinner.

items.title: Maverick and Farmer Coffee
items.why: A farm-to-cup coffee brand that grows its beans on its own 140-acre estate in Pollibetta, Coorg, and roasts them daily in Bengaluru. Have a filter coffee made with the estate beans and take a bag home.

items.title: Babai Tiffins
items.why: An Andhra vegetarian tiffin house cooking the food of the Krishna and Godavari deltas, and it insists it is not generically South Indian. Order pesarattu and ghee karam idli in the morning, or gongura rice later in the day.

items.title: Brik Oven
items.why: Neapolitan-style pizza on a sourdough base fermented for two to three days and fired at 400°C, with mozzarella made in-house every day. Order a margherita first: it shows off the cheese.

items.title: Light of Italy
items.why: An Italian kitchen that makes its own cheese and ice cream. Have pasta, then the gelato — the in-house work is the reason to choose it over the pizza places on 27th Main.

items.title: Sapna Book House
items.source: Wikipedia (Sapna Book House); branch position from OpenStreetMap
items.why: The Jayanagar branch of the bookseller Suresh Shah started near Majestic in 1967. Sapna has since become the largest Kannada-language publisher, and the Limca Book of Records listed it as India's largest bookstore. Come for the Kannada shelves, which few other shops can match, and for textbooks at ordinary prices.

items.title: Sreenivasa Brahmins Bakery
items.why: A family bakery on DVG Road since 1956, a few minutes' walk from Vidyarthi Bhavan and Gandhi Bazaar. It sells the old Bengaluru bakery range of buns, biscuits and savoury namkeen. Buy a bag of biscuits on the way to breakfast and eat them later with tea.

items.title: Glen's Bakehouse
items.why: A Bengaluru bakery café that has grown into a chain of about fifteen outlets in the city. The Koramangala branch is the neighbourhood's easy afternoon stop for a cake and a coffee. Go for a pastry rather than a meal.

items.title: CrossWord
items.why: A big chain bookshop on the lower ground floor of the Mantri Square mall. It is useful because it is large and open late, and it is next to the metro. Come for new releases and children's books, and go to an independent shop for anything you want to linger over.

items.title: Crossword
items.why: Whitefield's one large bookshop, an open-plan Crossword inside the Forum Value Mall. Come for new releases and children's books.

items.title: Chinita
items.area: Kiosk 1, Deck Floor, Campus 6B, RMZ Ecoworld
items.why: The Ecoworld kiosk of the Mexican kitchen that has been cooking from scratch in Bengaluru since 2012. It is the best lunch inside the tech park. Order tacos and eat them in the sun on the deck.

items.title: Biergarten
items.why: A brewpub in the German beer-garden style that brews its lagers, wheat beers and IPAs in-house. The Bellandur branch is its largest and leafiest, with long communal tables. Order the hefeweizen and a dunkel to compare, and come on a weekday evening.

items.title: Sharief Bhai
items.why: Dakhni biryani — the Deccan Muslim household style, sealed and slow-cooked on dum with short-grained jeerakasala rice. The chain began as a single Bengaluru kitchen in 2017. Order the mutton dum biryani; the kofta biryani is the unusual one.

items.title: Beijing Bites
items.why: Bengaluru's own Indian-Chinese neighbourhood chain, running for more than twenty years and with over thirty branches. Expect the city's version of Chinese food rather than China's. Order Hunan tofu and a plate of noodles for a cheap, reliable weeknight dinner.
